documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Spring check-in. Doing well. No bleeding, no dizziness, face normal. Prednisone 10 mg every morning, calcium three times a day (admits she often misses the midday one at school), D3 daily. Hematology in December unchanged, next visit in June.

Exam: BP fine, weight stable around 71. A few shin bruises. Face symmetric. No edema.

A/P
1. Chronic ITP on prednisone, hematology following.
2. Calcium: fine to take two doses at home if the midday one is hard; total about the same.
RTC fall physical.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
46 y/o, physical moved from November.

Interval: uneventful year. ITP stable on prednisone 10 mg daily, hematology December, no change. No bleeding. No vertigo since 2024; face normal since the 2023 Bell palsy. Calcium most days, D3 daily.

ROS: negative.

Exam: vitals as charted, weight steady. Face symmetric, eye closure full. A few small bruises on the shins, no petechiae. Heart RRR, lungs clear. Abdomen soft, no splenomegaly. Breast exam normal. No edema.

A/P
1. Chronic ITP on prednisone 10 mg, hematology following every 6 months. CBC today.
2. Long-term steroid: A1c, CMP, vitamin D today. DXA was 2021.
3. Health maintenance: FIT kit given (last negative 12/2024). Mammogram October normal. Pap 2023. Flu and COVID this fall done.
RTC September for a follow-up with fall labs.

documents.title: Face again
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Woke up and the right side of my face is weak again, same as 2023. Can't close my eye all the way. I'm getting over a cold. No other symptoms. I called the neurology office and they can see me tomorrow. Should I do anything today?

documents.title: Re: Face again
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Glad they can see you tomorrow. Today: protect the eye like last time (drops during the day, tape it at night). If you get weakness in an arm or leg, trouble speaking, vision change or a bad headache, call 911. Let me know what neurology recommends.

documents.title: Neurology Follow-up
documents.author: neurology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE NEUROLOGY PRACTICE
Return visit, seen 03/31/2026

47-year-old with chronic ITP on prednisone 10 mg daily and a right Bell palsy in 09/2023 that recovered completely. Yesterday morning the right face weakened again, much like the first time: she cannot close the right eye, lift the right brow or smile evenly. She is just over a cold. No rash, ear pain or tick exposure.

Meds: prednisone 10 mg daily, calcium carbonate 600 mg TID, vitamin D3 2000 IU daily. Allergies: NKDA.

Exam: complete right-sided facial paralysis including the forehead. No vesicles. Other cranial nerves normal. Limb strength and sensation normal. Gait normal.

Impression: recurrent right Bell palsy, same side as 2023.

Plan:
1. Prednisone 50 mg daily for 10 days in place of her 10 mg, then back to 10 mg; hematology aware.
2. Eye protection as before: carboxymethylcellulose drops while awake, gel and taping at night.
3. Because this is an ipsilateral recurrence, MRI of the brain and internal auditory canals with and without contrast.
4. Follow-up in 10 to 12 weeks.

reports.study: MRI brain and internal auditory canals with and without contrast
reports.text: Indication: recurrent right facial palsy. Technique: multiplanar multisequence MRI of the brain with thin-section imaging through the internal auditory canals, before and after intravenous gadolinium. Findings: brain parenchyma normal in signal and morphology. No mass, hemorrhage or abnormal enhancement. Ventricles and sulci normal for age. Facial and vestibulocochlear nerves normal in course and caliber bilaterally, with no abnormal enhancement of either facial nerve and no mass in the internal auditory canals or cerebellopontine angles. Parotid glands normal where imaged. Mastoids and middle ears clear.
reports.conclusion: Normal MRI of the brain and internal auditory canals. No lesion along either facial nerve.
